stem: A condition in which the body either does not produce enough insulin or cannot use it effectively, causing blood sugar (glucose) levels to remain abnormally high, is called:
explanation: Diabetes results from insufficient or ineffective insulin (a pancreatic hormone regulating blood glucose) — distinct from goitre (thyroid/iodine-related), anaemia (blood/iron-related), or rickets (a vitamin D/calcium deficiency affecting bones).

stem: A deficiency of iodine in the diet causes the thyroid gland to swell in the neck as it tries to compensate for insufficient thyroid hormone production. This visible swelling condition is called:
explanation: Goitre results from iodine deficiency, causing enlargement of the thyroid gland — this is why iodised salt is promoted as a public health measure — distinct from anaemia (iron deficiency), scurvy (Vitamin C deficiency), or night blindness (Vitamin A deficiency).

stem: A deficiency of iron in the diet reduces the body's ability to produce sufficient haemoglobin in red blood cells, leading to fatigue, weakness, and pale skin. This condition is called:
explanation: Iron-deficiency anaemia reduces haemoglobin production, impairing oxygen transport in the blood and causing fatigue and pallor — distinct from goitre (iodine deficiency) or osteoporosis (weakening of bones, often linked to calcium/Vitamin D deficiency in older age).
